subject: Reserved capacity commit: sizing scenarios and GPU-cost sensitivity
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@stellara.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-18 09:12 AM -0700
Subject: Reserved capacity commit: commit tenor and GPU-price sensitivity

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers look promising. Before we move to a formal term sheet, procurement has two asks we need you to help us model:

1) If we commit to a 24-month reserved pool, what happens to unit pricing if the market GPU index drops by 15-40%?
2) If there is a sudden spike in GPU costs, what protections can Redwood offer so our unit economics don't blow out (we need clear caps and triggers)?

We'd like a short matrix with 2–3 contract structures (anchored commit, phased ramp, and a hedge/escrow approach) showing: committed SKUs, monthly allocation, discount tiers, a price corridor, and what approvals are required to apply discretionary credits.

Can you share that by EOD Monday? Procurement will use this to compare with two other vendors.

Regards,
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Procurement, Stellara AI
[Stellara AI — procurement@stellara.ai]
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@stellara.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-18 11:03 AM -07:00
Subject: RE: Reserved capacity commit: commit tenor and GPU-price sensitivity

Samir — thanks for the clear asks. Attached is a first-pass spreadsheet with three operational scenarios as you requested:

• Anchored SKU (flat commitment, fixed discount bands, GPU-price corridor)
• Phased ramp (graduated activation with step-up discounts)
• Escrow/credit buffer (savings escrow that unlocks if index falls)

High level notes:
- We can offer a base discount tied to committed GPU-hours and a separate, small discretionary pool (exec-approved) for one-off market moves.
- For downside protection (index drops), we typically offer a rebate/escrow that returns a portion of paid commitment if market rates fall below a floor. That preserves throughput economics for Redwood while giving you downside relief.
- For upside shock (GPU price spikes), we can add a temporary relief clause: up to a 12% cap on pass-through for spikes under a 20% threshold, beyond which we trigger a negotiated interim credit and an emergency review (finance + sales).

I've flagged which items need internal approvals in column H of the spreadsheet. Please see attached: redwood_reserved_scenarios_v1.xlsx and a short one-pager (deal_term_summary.pdf).

If you like, we can run a quick 30-min call tomorrow to walk the matrix with procurement and finance.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Head of Sales – Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_reserved_scenarios_v1.xlsx]
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-18 14:20 PM -07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: pricing guardrails and approval path

Mina / Ben — looked through the spreadsheet. A couple of operational changes I recommend before we present to procurement:

1) Add a clear GPU-cost corridor definition: use a 3-month trailing index to avoid one-off ticks. If corridor stays >25% below our committed blended cost for two consecutive months, trigger the rebate/escrow release.
2) For the escrow option, we should specify a maximum escrow pool = 5% of committed spend for the first 12 months, stepping down after that. This limits our balance-sheet exposure.
3) Approvals: anything that uses >60% of the discretionary pool or >$200k of credits should require Marissa (rev ops) + finance lead sign-off.

I'll draft the approval ladder and add links to the HS record and the Drive doc. Kicking to Ben for sell-through language.

Related: Drive doc for the scenarios is at https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-redwood-scenarios and HubSpot: HS-98321.

-Karthik
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-19 08:45 AM -07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: discretionary discount cap and escalation

All — agree with Karthik's guardrails. A few pragmatic asks from sales leadership: 

• We can commit to the anchored SKU approach for 18–24 months, but front-load activation credits in the first 3 months to help their ramp.
• I can approve up to a 7% one-time discretionary credit for customer experience issues or onboarding hits, but anything beyond that needs Marissa and finance sign-off.
• Escalation trigger: if index moves (up or down) by more than 25% from the blended committed cost within a 60-day window, auto-escalate to execs and pause any automatic pass-throughs until we align.

Marissa — can you confirm you're OK to be on the approval path for >$200k credit usage?

Thanks,
Ben
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@stellara.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-19 12:10 PM -07:00
Subject: RE: Reserved capacity commit: commit tenor and GPU-price sensitivity

Samir — following up with a consolidated recommendation and next steps.

Summary (short):
• Our recommended default: 18-month anchored-SKU with a 5% escrow pool and a 3-month trailing GPU-cost corridor for index measurements. This balances balance-sheet risk with meaningful downside protection for you.
• Alternative: phased ramp if you prefer lower upfront commitment costs — smaller discounts initially, step-ups at 6 and 12 months.
• Escalation & approvals: discretionary credits capped at 7% without Marissa/finance approval; anything >$200k needs sign-off. Index moves >25% trigger exec escalation and temporary pause on auto-pass-throughs.

Next steps:
1) If this looks good, sign the one-pager and we will convert the preferred scenario into a term sheet (DocuSign link will follow).
2) We propose a 30-min call tomorrow 10am PT to walk finance and procurement through the corridor math.

I attached the spreadsheet and one-pager again for reference.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Head of Sales – Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
